verses.1: All the people gathered as one person at the open space before the Water Gate, and they said to Ezra the scribe, “Bring the Book of the Teaching of Moses, which the LORD has commanded for Israel.”
verses.2: So Ezra the priest, the scribe, brought the Teaching before the assembly—men, women, and all who could understand—and read it on the first day of the seventh month.
verses.3: From morning until midday, in the open space before the Water Gate, Ezra read aloud to the men, women, and those who could understand. All the people listened with their ears to the Book of the Teaching.
verses.4: Ezra the scribe stood on a wooden platform that had been built for the purpose. Standing beside him were Mattithiah, Shema, Azariah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah on his right, and Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbadana, Zechariah, Meshullam on his left.
verses.5: Ezra opened the Book and all the people stood up.
verses.6: Ezra blessed the LORD, the great God, and all the people answered, “Amen! Amen!” and bowed down with their faces to the ground in worship to the LORD.
verses.7: Then Joshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jeshua, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, and the Levites who taught the people stood and explained the Teaching to the people while they remained in place.
verses.8: They read from the Book of the Teaching of God, explaining it and giving understanding, so that the people could grasp what was being read.
verses.9: Nehemiah, the Tirshatha, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who taught the people said to all the people, “This day is holy to the LORD your God. Do not mourn or weep, for all the people were weeping when they heard the words of the Teaching.”
verses.10: He said to them, “Go, eat rich foods and drink sweet drinks, and send portions to those who have nothing. For this day is holy to our Lord. Do not be sad, for the joy of the LORD is your strength.”
verses.11: The Levites calmed all the people, saying, “Be still, for today is holy. Do not be sad.”
verses.12: So all the people went to eat, drink, and send portions to each other in great joy, because they had understood the words that had been taught to them.
verses.13: On the second day, the heads of the fathers’ houses of all the people, the priests, and the Levites gathered to Ezra the scribe to study the words of the Teaching.
verses.14: They found written in the Teaching that the LORD had commanded through Moses that the people of Israel should live in booths during the festival in the seventh month.
verses.15: And that they should proclaim and make known throughout their cities and in Jerusalem, “Go out to the mountain and bring olive branches, branches of a tree with thick leaves, myrtle branches, palm fronds, and branches of a leafy tree, to make booths, as it is written.”
verses.16: So the people went out and brought them, and each made booths on their roof, in their courtyards, in the courtyards of the house of God, and in the open spaces before the Water Gate and the open space before the Gate of Ephraim.
verses.17: The whole assembly of those returning from exile made booths and lived in them. For from the days of Joshua son of Nun, the people of Israel had never done this before. There was great joy indeed.
verses.18: From the first day to the last day, they read the Book of the Teaching of God day by day, and they kept the festival for seven days, and on the eighth day they held the solemn assembly, according to the rule.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "the Water Gate" refers to a specific gate in Jerusalem, likely the one mentioned elsewhere in Nehemiah.
- v. 14–15: The reference to "a tree with thick leaves" likely corresponds to the "willow" or "cedar" in the original, but the exact species is not specified.
- v. 17: "Joshua son of Nun" is an alternate reference to Joshua, consistent with the Hebrew Bible’s naming convention.

[2] So Ezra the priest, the scribe, brought the Teaching before the assembly—men, women, and all who could understand—and read it on the first day of the seventh month.  
[3] From morning until midday, in the open space before the Water Gate, Ezra read aloud to the men, women, and those who could understand. All the people listened with their ears to the Book of the Teaching.

[7] Then Joshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jeshua, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, and the Levites who taught the people stood and explained the Teaching to the people while they remained in place.  
[8] They read from the Book of the Teaching of God, explaining it and giving understanding, so that the people could grasp what was being read.  
[9] Nehemiah, the Tirshatha, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites who taught the people said to all the people, “This day is holy to the LORD your God. Do not mourn or weep, for all the people were weeping when they heard the words of the Teaching.”

[12] So all the people went to eat, drink, and send portions to each other in great joy, because they had understood the words that had been taught to them.  
[13] On the second day, the heads of the fathers’ houses of all the people, the priests, and the Levites gathered to Ezra the scribe to study the words of the Teaching.

[16] So the people went out and brought them, and each made booths on their roof, in their courtyards, in the courtyards of the house of God, and in the open spaces before the Water Gate and the open space before the Gate of Ephraim.  
[17] The whole assembly of those returning from exile made booths and lived in them. For from the days of Joshua son of Nun, the people of Israel had never done this before. There was great joy indeed.  
[18] From the first day to the last day, they read the Book of the Teaching of God day by day, and they kept the festival for seven days, and on the eighth day they held the solemn assembly, according to the rule.

- v. 1: "the Water Gate" refers to a specific gate in Jerusalem, likely the one mentioned elsewhere in Nehemiah.
